description:
Natural process Arabica Gayo; profile: “Madu kelulut, aroma buah-buahan tropika, manis seperti tebu, bau pisang yang harum…”
Arabica Gayo is a specialty, single-origin coffee from the Gayo Highlands in Central Aceh, Indonesia, known for its strong aroma, complex flavor, low acidity, and heavy body. It's a premium export commodity that grows in nutrient-rich volcanic soil, often using traditional, organic methods like using fermented coffee husks for compost. The coffee's unique characteristics, such as nutty, chocolaty, and caramelly notes, are attributed to the specific agro-climatic conditions and its "wet hulling" processing method.

name: Ethiopia Alo Chilaka Tamiru Tedesse Honey
description: Good Ethiopians are harder to come by these days, with climate change and an unpredictable political landscape affecting production. Yet Alo Coffee, founded by Tamiru Tadesse, has partnered with coffee professionals worldwide to produce some of the most remarkable Ethiopian coffees we’ve tasted including lots featured in Ethiopia’s Cup of Excellence. Grown at 2, 450m (which is really high for coffee cultivation), this coffee offers delicate white florals and a jammy mouthfeel. Comforting yet vibrant in every sip.

name: Ethiopia Bokissa Shakiso Guji G1 Natural
description:
We selected this natural Ethiopian coffee for its classic expression of what we love about the region; bright, floral, and fruit-forward. yet with a unique character of its own. Grown in the highlands of Guji, Oromia, this lot comes from Sookoo, a family-run organization with deep roots in Ethiopian coffee farming. Their dedication to quality and detail shines in the cup. Naturally processed, it carries rich sweetness and layered complexity, offering vibrant berry notes, a juicy, syrupy mouthfeel, and a smooth finish. Lively and expressive, it captures both the tradition and individuality of its origin.

*Shoutout to Daniel (who’s in Jakarta now) for delivering this coffee to us!

name: Malaysia MyLiberica Johor Jason Liew
description: MyLiberica is a Liberica farm in Simpang Renggam, Johor, just an hour from Batu Pahat. Owned by Jason Liew, the 50-acre farm is dedicated solely to Liberica and has invested in a processing facility for over a decade. This commitment has attracted barista competitors from around the world who explore Liberica in their presentations. The 2015 World Barista Champion , Sasa Sestic collaborated with MyLiberica in 2020 to develop an anaerobic process, transforming Liberica’s traditionally “muddy” profile into one with vibrant flavors. However, this particular coffee is sun-dried under controlled temperatures, highlighting its unique character: sweet, heavy-bodied, and rounded in mouthfeel.

name: Indonesia - Ijen East Java Kevenka Coffees Orange Bourbon
description:
Region: Ijen, East Java
Producer: Kevenka Coffees

Notes from Erika:

The Orange Bourbon variety is a rare Bourbon mutation, celebrated for its striking orange-coloured ripe cherries. This unique genetic trait, combined with Ijen’s rich volcanic soils, creates a coffee with a distinct and vibrant flavor profile. Unlike many Indonesian coffees, which often lean toward deep spices and darker notes, this coffee surprises with a fruit-forward, clean, and exceptionally sweet cup. The cherries underwent a 48-hour natural anaerobic fermentation, a process that amplifies their natural sweetness and adds a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel to the coffee. The result is a balanced cup that highlights the delicate fruit notes of blood orange and grapefruit.

name: Sweet Escape Blend Espresso
description: Enhances sweetness in your everyday long black or espresso.

name: The Work Of Art Blend
description: This blend was created with the intention to balance both sweetness and complex flavours to compliment each elements in your cup. Roasted medium which yields sugary sweetness and nutty flavours. Try it with your preferred milk or in your signature drink.

name: Ethiopia - Guji Gelena Geisha Washed
description:
Region: Guji
Producer: Gelena

Notes from Erika:

Grown in the highlands of Guji, this washed Gesha offers an expressive cup that showcases the finest qualities of its Ethiopian origin. As a variety originated from Ethiopia, it reflects the distinctive character of the terroir in which it was cultivated. This coffee shows off everything we love about the Gesha variety, it has a soft white-floral aroma that reminds us of jasmine. With notes of orange peel, it carries a lively acidity that adds vibrancy and structure to the cup. As it cools, the coffee settles into a clean and silky, tea-like finish. The result is a refreshing and layered drinking experience.

name: Honduras - Entre Caminos by Fernando Contreras
description:
Region: Montecillos
Producer: Entre Caminos by Fernando Contreras
Varietals: Icatu / Catuai

Notes from Erika:

Entre Caminos is a coffee farm managed by three generations of the Contreras family, situated in the mountain range of Montecillos. This naturally processed Catuai showcases delicate notes of cantaloupe and honey, layered with the smooth richness of milk chocolate. The natural processing imparts a gentle fruitiness that complements its creamy sweetness. Each sip is layered yet comforting, offering a warm and inviting drinking experience. This coffee is an easy-to-enjoy coffee with a sweet, mellow character.

name: SOE - Ethiopia Bekele Belachew G1 Haro Genet Lot 3 (Espresso)
description:
Region: Sagara Village, Bensa, Sidamo
Producer: Bekele Belachew
Altitude: 2000-2200m
Varietal: 74158, 74152
Process: Natural

Recently, we’ve noticed many Ethiopian coffees on the shelves featuring farmers’ names instead of processing or milling stations. We learned that there have been changes to Ethiopia’s export laws, allowing smallholder producers to market their coffees directly.

This coffee is produced by Bekele Belachaw, who owns 6 hectares of coffee in Sagara village in the Bensa district of Sidama. His six children and his wife all work on the farm. Most of the coffees they grow are the 74158 and 74160 varieties from the Jimma Research Centre. These varieties are resistant to diseases and are known for their pronounced citrus and floral notes.

When we cupped this coffee, we instantly fell in love with its citrusy flavors and sugary sweetness. We’ve been craving for a nice Ethiopian coffee and this coffee definitely hits the spot.

name: SOE - Guatemala Santa Felisa Blue Diamond SHB (Espresso)
description:
Producer: Anabella and Antonio Meneses
Process: Natural

Back in May, we had the privilege of hosting Anabella from Santa Felisa, Guatemala, for a coffee cupping and sharing session at the Bad Artist Coffee Co space. During the session, we learned about Santa Felisa’s approach to regenerative farming while maintaining the quality of their prized coffees.

Santa Felisa was established in 1904 in the Acatenango region and is currently run by siblings Anabella and Antonio Meneses. They are considered one of Guatemala’s pioneering specialty coffee producers, leading the origin’s pursuit of excellence.

We selected this coffee as our seasonal offering this month because it possesses a uniquely complex character of red and purple fruits such as cranberries, cherries, and grapes. As a black coffee, it showcases beautiful purple-toned flavours with a tea-like finish, and with milk, it reminds us of a lovely banoffee pie.

name: SOE - Indonesia Gayo Arkhan Sumatra Kampung Kenawat (Espresso)
description:
Region: Gayo Arkhan Sumatra
Producer: Kampung Kenawat
Altitude: 1200-1600m
Varietal: Typica, AB, Catimor, Hibrida de Timor
Process: Anaerobic Natural

Traditionally, Indonesian coffees are known for their heavy body and earthy, spice-like flavours. In the past, coffee producers in Indonesia processed their coffee using the traditional wet-hull method (giling basah). However, more young coffee professionals in the country are revolutionizing the industry by investing in better processing facilities and introducing new processing methods. As a result, we’re fortunate to have so many delicious varieties of Indonesian coffee on the market.

This particular coffee did not come easily, as the producing village, Kampung Kenawat, was severely affected by political movements and natural disasters. With much appreciation, we cupped this coffee with the coffee trader when they visited our space and were drawn to its complexity, which reminded us of local exotic fruits like salak. This coffee really shows its character from hot to cold, and we’re excited to see how it translates into both black and white espressos.

name: Cleanser
description:
A blend of carefully selected coffees from our premium and rare series from Latin America / Africa.

We’ve all been there, over-eating beyond our tummy capacity or too much of heavy food; an urge to lighten up the disgusted feeling follows. This coffee is the savior to refresh your mind, body, soul. Otherwise, it could be a good companion for a chillax afternoon tea.

name: Colombia Narino Geisha
description: Introducing our first Geisha from Narino, crafted by Henry, who recently made his mark in the Colombia National Quality Contest. This gem offers a crisp, clean cup with vibrant natural brightness, brought to life through the meticulous washed process. Its a silky mouthfeel and lingering, satisfying finish make it a true standout from this exceptional batch.

name: Brazil Castanhas
description:
Castanhas do Brasil (which means “Nuts of Brazil”) is a carefully curated blend from the Cocatrel Cooperative in Três Pontas, Minas Gerais. The cherries are sourced primarily from the Carmo de Cachoeira region in Sul de Minas, selected for their clean, sweet profile and scoring 83+ in quality evaluation.

The processing is done using static-box natural drying: cherries are dried in 1‑meter-deep ventilated boxes, with air circulating from below to ensure even drying without turning the fruit.On the fourth day of drying, the cherries are mixed to promote uniformity, then they rest for 1–2 weeks before being milled.

This method brings out a more fruit-forward sweetness than typical Brazilian naturals, while retaining a smooth, nutty body

Best brewing method:
☕️ Pour Over (V60 / Kalita) – highlights floral aromatics and clean acidity
🫖 Aeropress – brings out sweetness and body
🧊 Flash Brew / Iced Pour Over – refreshing with bright citrusy notes

name: Colombia Supremo
description: We love this bean especially early in the morning, as it provides the chocolate and caramel taste. If you are a person that likes a little kick in the butt in the morning, with a hint of chocolate, caramel, and green apple taste, this is the bean for you. Best of all, this bean is suitable for pour-over, normal brewing, french press, and also espresso.

name: Colombia Tolima Castillo Natural Winey
description: Sourced from the lush highlands of Tolima, Colombia, this lot is grown between 1, 200–2, 000 meters above sea level. The region’s volcanic soil, cool nights, and balanced rainfall nurture slow cherry development, resulting in deep sweetness and rich complexity. The Castillo variety — known for its resilience and vibrant flavor — thrives in this microclimate, producing exceptional quality when processed naturally.

name: El Salvador La Fany Red Bourbon
description:
Aroma (dry): Hibiscus, Tea-like, red plum
Flavour on sip: Gentle tea-like body with notes of hibiscus and juicy plum, complemented by subtle sweetness and clarity
Finish: Clean and elegant with a soft floral aftertaste that lingers pleasantly

Grown in the picturesque Apaneca-Illamatepec mountain range of El Salvador, this washed Red Bourbon lot comes from Finca La Fany, managed by the Silva Family. The farm sits between 1, 450 – 1, 550 masl, where cool mountain air and fertile clay-loam soils create ideal conditions for slow cherry maturation. With generations of experience, the Silva family’s careful cultivation brings out the elegant and balanced character that defines this coffee.

Processing
This lot is fully washed, meaning ripe cherries are pulped, fermented, and thoroughly washed before being dried on raised beds under the sun. The result is a clean, tea-like cup that highlights the Red Bourbon variety’s refined sweetness and delicate florals, with a smooth, silky texture.

name: Ethiopia G2 Mira Suke Kuto Lot
description:
Flavour on sip: Silky, tea-like body with juicy kyoho grape and cherry notes, complemented by delicate floral sweetness and clarity

Finish: Clean and elegant with a soft, lingering floral aftertaste

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Bogale Mengistu Wadera Natural G1
description: From the lush hills of the Yirgacheffe region in southern Ethiopia, this micro-lot is grown by farmer Bogale Mengistu Wadera at elevations around 2, 000 metres above sea level. The cool nights and sun-rich days ensure slow cherry maturation, allowing the beans to develop deep layers of fruit sweetness and refined acidity. Harvested by hand in his small-holder plots of heirloom varietals, this coffee is a testament to the land’s storied history of specialty coffee cultivation.

name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Red Honey G1
description:
Flavour on sip: Lemon custard sauce, white peach, Calpis-like brightness, finishing with honey sweetness and delicate coffee flower aroma

Finish: Sweet, refined and lingered with gentle citrus blossom

This coffee uses the Red Honey method — cherries are depulped but retain their mucilage, and the beans are dried with a high sugar content still intact. This creates a cup profile that is sweet and syrupy, layered with florals and delicate complexity, while maintaining the clean clarity that Yirgacheffe is celebrated for.

name: Genesis Espresso
description:
Our Genesis Blend is the perfect coffee for those seeking a rich, full-bodied cup with complex flavor notes. Crafted from two exceptional beans, Brazil Castanhas and Honduras this blend is designed with espresso and latte lovers in mind. However, its versatile profile can be enjoyed through any brewing method.

Together, these beans create a well-rounded, balanced cup with a rich body and a perfect combination of chocolate and caramel. As our first blend ever, Genesis Blend represents the beginning of our journey, and we're excited to share it with you. Enjoy a cup of Genesis Blend and experience the perfect harmony of two exceptional coffees!

name: Gesha Village Gori
description:
single-terroir lot comes from the Shewa-Jibabu block of the acclaimed Gesha Village Coffee Estate. Nestled on the edge of the Gori Gesha Forest in Ethiopia’s Bench Maji Zone, Gesha Village has become synonymous with meticulous cultivation, terroir-driven expression, and uncompromising quality.
This Gori Gesha Natural (Lot.24/099) reveals a vibrant and expressive cup. The dry aroma bursts with strawberry, mango, and floral notes, leading into a cup layered with strawberry and blackberry sweetness. Mid to finish, delicate accents of orange peel, grape, and toffee emerge, giving structure and complexity to the cup.
Crafted under the stewardship of Adam Overton and Rachel Samuel, Gesha Village continues to define the frontier of Ethiopian specialty coffee—connecting heritage, terroir, and innovation in every lot.

name: Give Back Blend
description:
Give Back Blend is our signature espresso roast crafted for comfort, richness, and everyday drinkability.

This blend brings together the chocolatey smoothness of Brazilian beans with the deep, earthy body of Sumatran coffee. The result is a bold, low-acid cup with notes of chocolate—balanced and full-bodied, perfect for both milk-based drinks and straight espresso.

Whether you're pulling a daily shot or making a weekend flat white, this blend delivers that classic, satisfying flavor you can count on.

Best For: Espresso, Milk-Based Drinks, Moka Pot

name: Midnight Shadow
description:
Say hello to Midnight Shadow, the coffee blend that's about to become your new best friend in the morning. We've handpicked the finest beans from Guatemala, and Brazil to create a bold and comforting cup that'll make you feel right at home.

Think of indulging in rich bittersweet chocolate, a touch of honey sweetness, and that comforting cacao flavor that fills you up just right. And the best part? It's not too sharp on the taste buds, so you can enjoy it without any puckering. Plus, the aftertaste? It's like a warm hug that lingers just a little longer.

Our team has put their heart and soul into roasting these beans to perfection, so you can experience that perfect, satisfying sip every single time. Embrace the shadows and let Midnight Shadow be that reliable, flavorful companion that's always there to brighten up your day.

name: Panama Abu 2260
description:
From the lush highlands of Boquete, Panama, this exceptional lot comes from the award-winning Abu Estate, renowned for producing some of the most elegant Geishas in the region. Grown at 1, 550 meters above sea level, the combination of terroir, altitude, and meticulous processing yields a cup of remarkable clarity and refinement.

This washed Gesha (#2260, air-shipped batch) opens with an enchanting aroma of lemon custard, peach, bergamot, and jasmine. On the palate, the cup is delicate yet expressive—layered with lemon custard, apricot, and jasmine, rounded by lingering notes of peach and bergamot. The result is a cup that embodies the classic Gesha profile: elegant, floral, and gracefully complex.

name: Panama Esmeralda Geisha Natural
description:
A rare treasure from the legendary Hacienda La Esmeralda, this auction-only Red Label lot represents the pinnacle of Geisha coffee. Harvested from the Cañas Verdes Farm, Montana Block, Lot.8NB showcases the unrivaled terroir and meticulous craftsmanship that have earned Esmeralda multiple Best of Panama awards and global recognition as one of the world’s most prestigious coffee producers.

This natural-processed Geisha bursts with layered complexity—radiant florals, vibrant tropical sweetness, and a silky, refined structure that defines the very essence of Esmeralda’s reputation. Reserved exclusively for the annual Esmeralda Auction, this lot embodies both rarity and excellence, offering a once-in-a-year opportunity to experience coffee at its most celebrated level.

Highlights:

Red Label Auction Lot – released only through Esmeralda Special Auction

Award-Winning Producer – multiple Best of Panama champion

Exceptional Terroir – Cañas Verdes Farm, Montana Block

Process: Natural

Varietal: Geisha

name: Revelation Blend
description:
Introducing the perfect blend for coffee lovers – 100% Arabica, no artificial flavoring, and roast level City+ to ensure a rich, smooth taste.

Featuring a tantalizing combination of Brazil Castanhas and Ethiopia Yirgacheffe , this blend delivers a unique taste experience with tasting notes of green apple, milk chocolate, and cane sugar. The natural process method ensures the flavors are authentic and pure.

Perfect for both filters and espresso, this blend offers a medium body and a medium acidity that's perfect for a daily cup. The espresso brings out the milk chocolate and the complexity of green apple, while the filter or v60 delivers a medium body and a jasmine aroma.

Experience the richness and complexity of HisBrew's coffee blend today. Order now and taste the difference.

name: Sumatra G1 DP Kenyalang
description: From the lush highlands of Sumatra, Indonesia, this coffee showcases the island’s hallmark Giling Basah (wet-hulled) tradition—an iconic post-harvest method that imparts its unmistakable character. The result is a cup with a rich, medium-to-thick body layered with notes of chocolate, warm spices, and subtle herbs, all tied together with a lingering sweetness.

name: Sumatra Gayo Mountain
description:
Love your coffee to be dark, with a slight bitterness? Try our first over Dark Roasted Sumatra Gayo Mountain. Made for those who crave dark roast, yet with minimum oiliness for your machines.

Why Sumatra? Because this is our first dark roasted arabica coffee! This coffee is from the region of Sumatra, sourced and graded for its consistency. It is roasted till the second crack, with a dark roast, that suits those who love their coffee dark, strong, and with a slight hint of bitterness to taste the KAO-ness.

This single origin is best consumed with just black coffee. If you use a Moka pot and love dark roasted coffee. This is made especially for you.

name: Bensa Bombe #2
description: Bensa Bombe #2 — A single-origin Ethiopian coffee from Sidamo and West Arsi, grown by Tariku Kare Banata. Handpicked and processed as Grade 1 naturals and washed lots, it offers a sweet, balanced cup with winey spice and classic Sidama brightness.

name: El Descanso
description: El Descanso — A single-origin coffee from Guadalupe, Huila, grown by Jose Heider Contreras. Handpicked and carefully washed, it delivers a sweet, complex cup that reflects the region’s rich character.

name: El Diviso Sidra
description: El Diviso Sidra — A single-origin Colombian coffee from southern Huila, showcasing the Sidra variety’s vibrant, layered flavours, crafted with meticulous processing by the Lasso family.

name: La Huaca
description: La Huaca — A single-origin Peruvian coffee from Cajamarca, grown by José Nicanor Zurita at 1, 900 meters. Naturally processed, it showcases the region’s clarity, sweetness, and José’s steady craftsmanship.

name: Lenin Flores
description: Lenin Flores — A single-origin Peruvian coffee from San Ignacio, grown at Finca El Morito by a third-generation producer. Carefully crafted from farm to post-harvest, it offers notes of pomelo, nutmeg, brown tea, and a clean finish.

name: Magarrissa Tulise
description: Magarrissa Tulise — A single-origin coffee from Gedeo near Yirgacheffe, sourced from 600 smallholders. Grown in biodiverse highlands and processed at Tulise Washing Station, it delivers a floral, vibrant, and expressive cup.

name: Ndiaini AA

description:
Processing Method: Peach-infused Anaerobic Honey (5 days in CO₂ tanks, 3 days co-fermented with real peach juice, then honey-style drying)
A bold departure from traditional processes, achieved via layered fermentation.

Brewing Recommendation: Filter Brews / Modern Espresso 

We implore coffee drinkers to think of modern fermentation and/or processing methods like a meticulously planned engineering process - just that what's being engineered is the complex world of flavours. It is thanks to these boundary-pushing coffee pioneers that we now understand more about the reason many specialty coffees are what they are, and we can now control the variables rather than leaving the results to fate and weather.

La Luisa's Innovation
This coffee is is a bold departure from traditional washed or natural processes, with layered fermentation method where cherries spend 5 days in CO₂ tanks, followed by 3 more days co-fermented with real peach juice before drying in honey-style (skins and flesh removed, leaving only the sticky mucilage). 

Some purists may raise an eyebrow to innovation, but to those who live where curiosity meets coffee, this is not a coffee to be missed.

name: Colombia Las Margarita "Hami Melon" CO2 A. Honey
description:
Flavor infusion using a pressurized Supercritical Fluid CO2 to ensure flavor reaches the core of the bean.

Forget artificial syrups and surface coatings; this is flavor infusion the next-level way—a geeky, brilliant process that lets us lock in phenomenal, pure taste.

Supercritical CO2
This method essentially uses a pressurized fluid to drive flavor deep inside the coffee bean. The process starts by taking CO2 and controlling its heat and pressure to create a Supercritical Fluid CO2. In this unique state, the CO2 can dissolve flavor like a liquid but penetrate matter like a gas.

A clean, natural flavor extract is dissolved into this CO2 carrier. When this solution is introduced to the coffee beans, the fluid quickly diffuses into all the microscopic pores, ensuring the flavor reaches the core of the bean, rather than just staying on the surface.

The final, essential step involves rapidly dropping the pressure. The CO2 instantly turns back into a gas and harmlessly escapes, leaving zero residue. The flavor molecules, having nowhere to go, are then perfectly deposited and locked within the bean's structure, resulting in a consistent and deeply infused product.

Processing Method: Double Anaerobic Honey (Yeast)
Adventurous coffee with an intensely berry profile. Profile achieved using a Yeast Double Anaerobic Honey method.

Experience a coffee unlike any other - Blueberry Reverie from Costa Rica Tarrazu is an adventurous coffee that’s perfect for those who crave a unique and vibrant cup. This light roast coffee offers a intensely berry profile that will redefine your brewing experience.

The Flavor Journey
Each sip is a trip to a berry patch, beginning with a burst of mixed berry and blueberry juice that's both sweet and complex. As the coffee cools, notes of bright tangerine emerge, cutting through the sweetness with a zesty citrus finish. Finally, a silky honey sweetness ties everything together, leaving a smooth, lingering aftertaste.

What's the Magic Behind?
This exceptional profile is achieved through a unique Yeast Double Anaerobic Honey processing method which carefully controls the fermentation with selected yeast strains to generate the flavour combination required to remind drinkers of blueberries. The notes are then imbued into the coffee during the second stage anaerobic fermentation. The result is a true testament to the innovation happening in the advancement of modern coffee processing techniques.

If you love exploring new flavors and appreciate a coffee with an undeniably fruity character, the Blueberry Reverie is made for you.

name: Costa Rica Rivense Chirripo Black Honey Geisha
altitude: 1700 masl tasting notes : hibiscus, red apple, honey about the coffee : Geisha from Café Rivense, a family-run farm and micromill in the Chirripó micro-region at 1,700 MASL. The black honey process — where most of the fruit mucilage is left on during drying — pushes the sweetness forward without muddying the varietal clarity. What you get is hibiscus and red apple up front, a clean honey sweetness through the mid, and a finish that lingers longer than you'd expect. Delicate but not shy

name: El Salvador Los Pirineos Orange Pacamara Washed
altitude: 1600 masl tasting notes : orange blossom, grapes, apricot about the coffee : Orange Pacamara is a large-bean mutation of Pacamara selected for its fruit-forward character, and Los Pirineos on the Tecapa volcano in Usulután is one of the farms that does it best. This lot delivers orange blossom and apricot upfront, with a grape-like sweetness that lingers. The washed process keeps it clean and precise. Light-roasted for filter. Floral, fruit-driven, and structured

name: Ethiopia Abdo Abamecha G1 Badeyi Lot 11
altitude: 2200 masl tasting notes : white floral, stone fruit, black tea about the coffee : Abdo Abamecha farms roughly 30 hectares in Badeyi, Limu Jimma at up to 2200 MASL — one of the higher plots in the region. The JARC varietals 74110 and 74112 grown here are known for clean floral expression, and this washed G1 lot delivers on that: white florals, stone fruit, and a dry black tea finish. Structured and precise without being austere. A straightforward filter coffee that doesn't ask much of you

name: Honduras Finca Gosen H-27 Anaerobic Natural
altitude: 1500 masl tasting notes : tropical fruits, cherry, raisin about the coffee : Mariano Nolasco farms Finca Gosen at 1500 MASL in La Pilas, a mountain community in Honduras where his family has worked the land for two generations. The H-27 varietal processed anaerobically — whole cherries fermented without oxygen — pushes the fruit forward in a way a standard natural won't. Expect tropical fruits, cherry, and raisin with real depth. Big, expressive, and built for filter

name: Kenya Thageini Lot 0424 CM Washed Diamond
altitude: 1750 masl tasting notes : roselle, blackcurrant, sugarcane about the coffee : Thageini wet mill sits within the Aguthi Farmers Cooperative in Nyeri, where around 450 smallholder members deliver cherry for collective processing. The CM washed method extends fermentation under controlled conditions, which pushes clarity and acidity without stripping body. SL28 and SL34 grown at this altitude tend toward bold fruit and firm structure, and that holds here. Expect roselle and blackcurrant upfront with a sugarcane sweetness that lingers and smooths the finish. Precise, expressive, and consistent across the cup

name: Peru Felipe Marin Mirez Geisha Natural La Palma
altitude: 1900 masl tasting notes : mango, hawthorn, milk chocolate about the coffee : Geisha from Peru are still rare, and Felipe Marin's lot from La Palma, Jaén earns the attention. At 1900 MASL, the Marin family farms alongside their father Silvestre, selecting cherries at peak ripeness and processing naturally at altitude. The result is precise and expressive: mango and hawthorn up front, with milk chocolate grounding the finish. It's a Geisha that doesn't overreach. Clean, sweet, and quietly confident

name: BRAZIL CERRADO
description: Cerrado is a vast tropical and subtropical biome that includes forests, marshlands and grassland. Covering more than 20 percent of Brazil, it is the largest savannah in South America. The name cerrado translates as closed, and the region remained so until the 1960s, when farmers began treating the soil. Over the last 40 years, the Cerrado has played a crucial role as Brazil has developed into a world economic power. Many farms and ranches of various sizes are located in the Cerrado, but it is the large-scale farms that supply the majority of the country's commercially raised agricultural products. Our Brazil Cerrado coffee is a high quality Brazilian bean - when roasted to medium or dark can bring out an ample, smooth body with nutty flavor. This particular coffee is also excellent for blending.

The fully washed process enhances clarity and structure, resulting in a cup that is approachable, consistent, and versatile across brew methods. In the cup, it opens with bright orange acidity, followed by juicy raspberry sweetness. A smooth milk chocolate note rounds out the profile, giving a balanced body and a soft, comforting finish that makes it equally enjoyable as filter or espresso.

name: ETHIOPIA BUKU SAYISA TIKUYA
description: Description Buku Sayisa Washing Station is located in the highlands of Guji, Ethiopia, at elevations of 2,100–2,350 meters above sea level, an ideal environment for producing dense, high-quality coffee. Named after an Amharic phrase meaning “blessed valley,” the station works with around 450 smallholder farmers growing indigenous Ethiopian Arabica varieties, preserving the region’s rich coffee heritage while delivering consistent specialty-grade lots. Both washed and natural coffees are produced at Buku Sayisa. Washed lots are pulped and fermented under water for 36–72 hours before being dried on raised beds for 7–10 days, while natural lots are dried as whole cherries for 12–15 days to ensure controlled fermentation. description: Description Honduras Copán Fully Washed comes from the western highlands of Honduras, a region well known for producing smooth and balanced coffees. Grown by smallholder farmers at higher elevations, the cherries ripen slowly, helping to create a naturally sweeter and more rounded flavour. The fully washed process brings out a clean and consistent cup that is easy to enjoy and reliable for everyday drinking. In the cup, this espresso offers a comforting and familiar taste experience. Soft stone fruit sweetness leads the way, followed by creamy milk chocolate that gives a rich and smooth body. Gentle hazelnut notes appear at the finish, adding warmth and a pleasant aftertaste. Approachable and versatile, this coffee works beautifully as a straight espresso and pairs effortlessly with milk for a satisfying daily cup.

description: From the sub-region of Lake Takengon, Sumatra Mandheling is a wet-hulled coffee that provides your coffee cup with a heavy and complex body. Sumatra Mandheling tasting notes often describe it as earthy and intense with an herbal aroma, unique to the region and not found in South American or African coffees. With just enough acidity to provide a vibrancy, Mandheling coffee often exhibits tones of sweet chocolate and licorice.

name: ROMA BLEND
altitude: clarity and sun-dried sweetness. This blend is a masterclass in balance, meticulously crafted to bridge the gap between the clean, crisp profiles of Central America and the wild, fruit-forward intensity of East Africa. The Composition We’ve paired two contrasting processes to create a multi-dimensional flavor profile: 50% Honduras (Washed Process): Provides the "spine" of the blend. The washed process ensures a clean, sparkling body and highlights the deep, chocolatey structure of the cacao notes. 50% Ethiopia (Natural Process): Adds the "soul" and sweetness. By drying the coffee cherry whole, we’ve preserved the intense sugars that translate into those unmistakable tropical and stone fruit characteristics. From the first sip, ROMA BLEND greets you with a bright, crystalline acidity reminiscent of starfruit . As the cup warms, it unfolds into a lush medley of tropical fruits —think mango and pineapple sweetness—all grounded by a sophisticated, velvet-like finish of cacao nibs . It is a vibrant, complex coffee that remains approachable whether brewed as a pour-over or a bright, modern espresso.
